QUESTION: For a projective variety $X\subseteq\mathbb{P}^n$ and a linear subspace $V\subseteq\mathbb{P}^n$, how is the polar variety $P(X,V)$ defined?

ATOM: For a variety $X\subseteq\mathbb{P}^n$ and a subspace $V\subseteq\mathbb{P}^n$, the polar variety is $P(X,V)=\{p\in \mathrm{Reg}(X)\setminus V \mid V+p \text{ intersects } X \text{ at } p \text{ non-transversely}\}$.
KEY POINTS:
1. It is the set of regular points $p$ of $X$ that do not lie in $V$
2. with the condition that the span $V+p$ meets $X$ at $p$ non-transversely

ANSWER TO GRADE:
The polar variety \(P(X,V)\) is the Zariski closure in \(X\) of the smooth points \(x\) where the embedded tangent space \(T_xX\) meets \(V\) nontransversely:
\[
P(X,V)=\overline{\left\{x\in X_{\mathrm{sm}}:\dim(T_xX\cap V)\ge \dim X+\dim V-n+1\right\}}.
\]
